name.text: Two-secant theorem - find PD and the chord CD (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
From an external point \(P\), two secants are drawn to a circle. The first secant meets the circle at \(A\) and \(B\), with \( PA = {@PA@} \) cm and \( AB = {@AB@} \) cm. The second secant meets the circle at \(C\) and \(D\), with \( PC = {@PC@} \) cm.

[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="430px"]] var PA = {#PA#}, PB = {#PB#}, PC = {#PC#}, PD = {#ta_pd#}; var rad = Math.PI / 180; var u1 = [Math.cos(158 * rad), Math.sin(158 * rad)]; var u2 = [Math.cos(202 * rad), Math.sin(202 * rad)]; var Pp = [0, 0]; var Ap = [PA * u1[0], PA * u1[1]], Bp = [PB * u1[0], PB * u1[1]]; var Cp = [PC * u2[0], PC * u2[1]], Dp = [PD * u2[0], PD * u2[1]]; function circum(p1, p2, p3) { var x1 = p1[0], y1 = p1[1], x2 = p2[0], y2 = p2[1], x3 = p3[0], y3 = p3[1]; var d = 2 * (x1 * (y2 - y3) + x2 * (y3 - y1) + x3 * (y1 - y2)); var cx = ((x1*x1 + y1*y1) * (y2 - y3) + (x2*x2 + y2*y2) * (y3 - y1) + (x3*x3 + y3*y3) * (y1 - y2)) / d; var cy = ((x1*x1 + y1*y1) * (x3 - x2) + (x2*x2 + y2*y2) * (x1 - x3) + (x3*x3 + y3*y3) * (x2 - x1)) / d; return [cx, cy]; } var ctr = circum(Ap, Bp, Cp); var rr = Math.hypot(ctr[0] - Ap[0], ctr[1] - Ap[1]); var pad = 1.2; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [ctr[0] - rr - pad, ctr[1] + rr + pad, Math.max(ctr[0] + rr, 0) + pad + 0.6, ctr[1] - rr - pad], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); board.create('circle', [ctr, rr], {strokeColor: '#178a8a', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [Pp, Bp], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [Pp, Dp], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); var A = board.create('point', Ap, {name: 'A', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [2, 12], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'bottom'}}); var B = board.create('point', Bp, {name: 'B', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [-4, 12], anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'bottom'}}); var C = board.create('point', Cp, {name: 'C', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [4, -12], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'top'}}); var D = board.create('point', Dp, {name: 'D', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [-4, -12], anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'top'}}); var P = board.create('point', Pp, {name: 'P', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [10, 0], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle'}}); function lbl(p1, p2, dy, txt) { board.create('text', [(p1[0] + p2[0]) / 2, (p1[1] + p2[1]) / 2 + dy, txt], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 13, fixed: true, cssStyle: 'color:#333'}); } lbl(Pp, Ap, 0.8, PA + ' cm'); lbl(Ap, Bp, 0.8, PB - PA + ' cm'); lbl(Pp, Cp, -0.8, PC + ' cm'); [[/jsxgraph]]
(a) Find \( PD = \) [[input:ans1]]\(\text{ cm}\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
(b) Hence find the chord length \( CD = \) [[input:ans2]]\(\text{ cm}\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
We are told \(PA\) and \(AB\), so first find the whole distance from \(P\) to \(B\):

\[ PB = PA + AB = {@PA@} + {@AB@} = {@PB@}\text{ cm}. \]

By the two-secant theorem, \( PA\cdot PB = PC\cdot PD \), so

\[ {@PA@}\times{@PB@} = {@PC@}\times PD \quad\Rightarrow\quad PD = \frac{{@PA@}\times{@PB@}}{{@PC@}} = {@ta_pd@}\text{ cm}. \]

The chord \(CD\) is the part of the second secant inside the circle:

\[ CD = PD - PC = {@ta_pd@} - {@PC@} = {@ta_cd@}\text{ cm}. \]

questionvariables.text: /* Randomise (PA, AB, PC); PB = PA + AB; require PA*PB divisible by PC so PD is a whole number. PC < PD keeps P external with C the near point; PC # PA keeps the two secants distinct; CD >= 2; lengths bounded. Generated on the fly. */ quads : sublist( create_list([pa,ab,pc], pa,2,8, ab,3,14, pc,2,9), lambda([z], is( integerp(z[1]*(z[1]+z[2])/z[3]) and z[3] < z[1]*(z[1]+z[2])/z[3] and z[3] # z[1] and z[1]*(z[1]+z[2])/z[3] - z[3] >= 2 and z[1]+z[2] <= 20 and z[1]*(z[1]+z[2])/z[3] <= 24 and z[1]*z[2] # z[1]*(z[1]+z[2])/z[3] ))); /* PA*AB # PD, so the raw-product slip is detectable */ sel : rand(quads); PA : sel[1]; AB : sel[2]; PC : sel[3]; PB : PA + AB; ta_pd : PA*PB/PC; /* PD */ ta_cd : ta_pd - PC; /* chord CD */ wrong_useAB : PA*AB/PC; /* used AB instead of PB: PA*AB = PC*PD */ wrong_rawprod : PA*AB; /* multiplied PA*AB and gave that as PD (no divide by PC) */ wrong_chord_pd : PC + PA*AB/PC; /* used the chords: PA*AB = PC*CD, so PD = PC + PA*AB/PC */

node.description: Used AB instead of PB (forgot PB = PA + AB).

truefeedback.text: It looks like you used \(AB\) as the second length. But \(PB\) is the whole distance from \(P\) to \(B\), so work out \(PB = PA + AB\) first, then apply \(PA\cdot PB = PC\cdot PD\). Try again.

node.description: Multiplied PA*AB and gave it as PD (used AB, and did not divide by PC).

truefeedback.text: It looks like you worked out \(PA\times AB\) and used that as \(PD\). Two things to fix: the first secant's product is \(PA\times PB\) with \(PB = PA + AB\) (not \(AB\)); and that product equals \(PC\times PD\), so you must divide by \(PC\) to get \(PD\). Try again.

node.description: Used the chords: PA*AB = PC*CD, giving PD = PC + PA*AB/PC.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you applied the theorem to the chords inside the circle, as \(PA\cdot AB = PC\cdot CD\). The two-secant theorem instead uses the whole secants measured from \(P\): \(PA\cdot PB = PC\cdot PD\), where \(PB = PA + AB\) and \(PD\) is the full distance from \(P\) to \(D\). Set it up that way and try again.

falsefeedback.text: Use the two-secant theorem \(PA\cdot PB = PC\cdot PD\), remembering that \(PB = PA + AB\). Form the equation and solve for \(PD\). Have another go.

truefeedback.text: That is \(PD - PC\) using your value of \(PD\), so your method is right — but your \(PD\) is not correct yet. Fix part (a), then subtract \(PC\) again.

node.description: Gave PD (the whole secant length) instead of the chord CD.

truefeedback.text: That is \(PD\), the whole distance from \(P\) to \(D\). The chord \(CD\) is only the part inside the circle: \(CD = PD - PC\). Subtract \(PC\) and try again.

falsefeedback.text: The chord \(CD\) is the part of the secant inside the circle, \(CD = PD - PC\). Once you have \(PD\), subtract \(PC\). Try again.
